Early skips are weak negative evidence. AI downweighting requires repeated skips, not a single event.
Repeated qualified listening provides behavioral evidence of continued interest.
Playback reached its end with at least 80% of the duration actually heard, a stronger signal than a brief play.

Basis: your endorsed reference library. A modest weight is used, with album size balanced.
New-music search directions retained: %1$d. Ranking also considers novelty, recent repetition and exploration; it does not guarantee a particular artist on every visit.
Reference tracks: %1$d · Favorites: %2$d · Legacy qualified plays: %3$d. References indicate broad taste; they are not counted as favorites or listening history.
Audio excerpts analyzed · Tracks: %1$d · Total seconds: %2$d. The following describes only those excerpts.

Excerpt features are model observations, not human-verified facts. They do not establish the sound of whole songs, other tracks, or your genre preferences. Titles are never used to infer genre, mood, rhythm or instrumentation.

Qualified listen: at least 30 seconds heard, or half of a short track.
High completion: playback ended naturally and at least 80% was heard.
Early skip: intentional track change before 30 seconds and 25% of the duration; 30 seconds is used if duration is unknown.
Pauses, failures and normal stops are not negative feedback. Sessions crossing midnight are assigned by their last report date. Collections use the full recording duration.
